title: Hold wide merge for standalone Uniform at the late admission boundary
question: Can the wider terminal merge transfer safely to standalone Uniform?
summary: Three verified native pairs save 9.231–12.321 seconds, but a matched late peer allows snapshot encoding and yields a typed sink denial with the widened cursor.

workloads: 8 GiB standalone Uniform Shuffle, one worker and explicit 256 MiB, WSL2 ext4 and ordinary host headroom.

validation.summary: Seven exact-cap CSVs, manifest, IDs/fields and cleanup pass in each timed arm. Both modes admit the same peer in the 96-run test. Only the existing path completes encoding. Denial releases staging and tracked capacity.

limitations: One synthetic 8 GiB cohort. The shared-owner regression is a focused cursor/encoding component test.
The separate 1 GiB hard-cgroup baseline attempt denied admission before publication.
exclusions: Native Windows, WASI, physical device I/O, and wider replay guarantees.
reopen_when: Prove a measured terminal cursor and final-writer owner that completes under the same admitted competitor requests, then repeat matched usable output timing.
